_comment: Hand-authored album metadata. The tuning system lives in the DIRECTORY name and nowhere in the filenames, so it cannot be derived — it has to be recorded here. `scripts/build-catalog.mjs` merges this with the track lists scanned from ~/Dropbox/Uploads and writes src/data/catalog.json, which IS committed (Cloudflare's build machine has no Dropbox access).
_order: Key order in `tunings` drives section order on /listen. Albums are sorted by date, newest first, within each section.

albums.title: Allow staccato woodwinds along with the a new set of chorales 391-402
End of August 2026
albums.blurb: Modified durations to include simpler rhythm patterns.

albums.title: Chorale Preludes
albums.blurb: A full chorale prelude based on the latest tuning runs.

albums.title: Just the Chorale
albums.blurb: A short-repeats pass after six episodes of heavy compute, 12 hours of annealing and Viterbi, to see if the chorale itself can be made to sound better. The answer is yes, but at the cost of a few cents of extra movement between adjacent chords.

albums.title: Late August 2026
albums.blurb: A short-repeats pass on a new tuning search that closes the gap in cents between adjacent chords to zero or near zero, at the cost of slightly higher integer-ratio scores.

albums.title: Minimal Movement
albums.blurb: Optimized for minimal movement of cent values between adjacent chords with common pitch classes. The first of the d series.

albums.title: Short Repeats
albums.blurb: A structural variant of the late-June pass, with the repeats shortened.

albums.title: June 2026
albums.blurb: The first full pass in One Footed Bride Tuning.

albums.title: Werckmeister III
albums.blurb: The same twelve chorales in a well temperament of Bach's own era — a reference point between equal temperament and just intonation.

albums.title: 12-Tone Equal Temperament
albums.blurb: The control. The same twelve chorales in the tuning of every modern piano, for direct comparison.

albums.title: Early Experiments
albums.blurb: The first attempts, at markedly slower tempos.

just.label: One Footed Bride Tuning
just.description: A just-intonation system of my own. Chords tuned to whole-number frequency ratios drawn from a tonality diamond, found by simulated annealing and then threaded together with Viterbi optimisation. These are successive passes at the same idea, newest first — each refines the tuning search and the orchestration over the one before it.

werckmeister.label: Werckmeister III
werckmeister.description: A well temperament from 1691, contemporary with Bach. Keys retain distinct character rather than sounding identical.

12tet.label: 12-tone equal temperament
12tet.description: The modern standard: the octave split into twelve identical steps. Every key is equally usable and no chord is perfectly in tune.

early.label: Early experiments
early.description: The first renders, made before the density control existed — they use the legacy max-shift setting and much slower tempos. Kept for reference; superseded by the One Footed Bride Tuning passes above.
